name: Votoplam
summary: Votoplam (PTC518) is an oral HTT pre-mRNA splicing modifier that lowers huntingtin protein. Novartis licensed it from PTC in December 2024 for $1.0bn upfront, with a 40/60 US profit share and ex-US royalties. The pivotal trial is INVEST-HD (NCT07326709): 770 early-stage patients aged 21 to 70 (CAG of 40 or more, TFC 13, TMS 7 to 25), randomised 3:2 to 10 mg or placebo for up to three years. The primary endpoint is cUHDRS progression and primary completion is 2030-04. Price anchor, a judgement: no disease-modifying HD drug exists, so the anchor is Skyclarys, the first oral disease-modifying drug in a rare inherited neurodegeneration, at $266,507 per 2024 Part D beneficiary. Eligible share, peak penetration and discontinuation are left null: no source measures the early-stage share of US HD, and no disease-modifying HD drug has launched to measure uptake against.

therapy_mode.source: INVEST-HD (NCT07326709): votoplam 10 mg or placebo once daily for up to three years (Rare Disease Advisor, 'Votoplam Enters Phase 3 Trial for Early Symptomatic Huntington Disease'). The PIVOT-HD extension (NCT06254482) runs to 2029
therapy_mode.note: A daily oral that slows a progressive disease, taken indefinitely

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Skyclarys: CMS Medicare Part D 2024, $101,272,751 over 380 beneficiaries = $266,507 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement, a departure from the house convention. The only marketed drugs in HD treat chorea, a symptomatic setting. Ingrezza, which carries an HD chorea label but is mostly used for tardive dyskinesia, is $60,819 per 2024 Part D beneficiary; Austedo is not in the book's demand data. Skyclarys is the closest pricing analogue: an oral, first disease-modifying therapy for a rare inherited neurodegeneration. Case against: HD has about 4x Friedreich ataxia's diagnosed US population (about 22,000 against about 5,000), and a larger pool usually prices lower. Evrysdi, another oral splicing modifier, is higher at $328,087. Taking Ingrezza under the convention would cut the price 77%

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention on a CMS per-beneficiary price (halving lands at a median 96% of CMS negotiated net prices; backend/gross_to_net.py)
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 0.5 off list, so net is $133,254 per patient-year. Case against: a first-in-class rare-disease drug with no competitor usually carries far smaller rebates than a competitive class. The halving partly corrects for part-year beneficiaries rather than rebates

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.note: Null: votoplam has no published retention or treatment-duration figure (PIVOT-HD extension Month 24 reports efficacy, not dropout), and no disease-modifying HD drug is marketed to borrow from. Chorea drugs are symptomatic and not comparable

forecast_start_year.source: NCT07326709 primary completion 2030-04-02 (ClinicalTrials.gov, last update 2026-09-22); readout expected 2030 (BioSpace, 'Novartis, PTC push Huntington's drug into Phase 3, mum on accelerated approval')
forecast_start_year.note: Book convention: the first full year is two calendar years after the pivotal primary completion. Case for earlier: an accelerated approval on PIVOT-HD's mHTT lowering, which Novartis has not ruled out or confirmed

exus_multiple.source: Kesimpta FY2025: $1,483mm rest of world against $2,943mm US (Novartis 20-F FY2025, 0001114448-26-000004, net sales by product)
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator. Kesimpta is Novartis's largest chronic neuroscience drug with a clean filed split. Case against: it is a multiple sclerosis drug in a large market. Zolgensma, Novartis's rare-neurology product, runs at 1.98x ($819mm against $413mm), but it is a one-time therapy whose US pool is used up. HD prevalence is similar in Europe and far lower in East Asia

economics_share.source: PTC Therapeutics 8-K (0001070081-24-000029), 2 December 2024, and PTC's 10-K: PTC receives $1.0bn upfront, up to $1.9bn in milestones, a 40% share of US profits and losses, and tiered double-digit royalties on ex-US sales
economics_share.note: Judgement: a blend. Novartis keeps 60% in the US and (1 - royalty) ex-US. With the Kesimpta ex-US multiple of 0.504 and a royalty at the 10% floor of 'double-digit': (0.6 + 0.504 x 0.9) / 1.504 = 0.70. At a 20% royalty the share is 0.667, and 0.6 if the ex-US royalty were ignored. The tiers are not disclosed, so 0.70 is an upper bound. Milestones are not netted here

prevalence.source: Age-adjusted diagnostic frequency of 6.52 per 100,000 in a 67-million-enrollee US claims database, 2003-2016 (Bruzelius et al., Mov Disord 2019;34:858, PMID 30868663, doi:10.1002/mds.27653). Applied to the 340,110,988 US residents of 1 July 2024 (Census Vintage 2024 national estimate)
prevalence.note: Diagnosed patients, which is the pool a label can reach. Estimates of the true count, including the undiagnosed, run to about 41,000. The book carries no HD pool (pool lookup empty). The Census total is quoted from the Vintage 2024 release and should be checked by the second reader

incidence.source: Same study: age-adjusted incidence 1.22 per 100,000 (PMID 30868663), applied to 340,110,988
incidence.note: The abstract's printed confidence intervals do not bracket either point estimate, a typo in the source. The point estimates are used

eligible_pct.note: Null. INVEST-HD enrols early manifest patients with TFC 13 (the maximum), TMS 7 to 25, UHDRS-IS of at least 90 and age 21 to 70. No source found gives the share of diagnosed US HD patients who meet this. Enroll-HD analyses (e.g. 'Total functioning capacity scale in Huntington's disease: natural course over time', PMID 39812810) describe TFC trajectories but do not report the cut. A label may also be broader than the trial

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of each year's eligible patients
penetration_peak_pct.note: Null. No disease-modifying HD drug has launched. The closest analogue, Skyclarys, has no filed US patient count on therapy (Biogen reports revenue, $520.5mm worldwide in 2025, not patients), and its Part D count (380) is only Medicare's slice of a young population. So no share can be solved back without a guessed denominator

ramp_steepness.source: book: trontinemab seed, fitted to Leqembi's three-point Part B new-start series (k 1.0396, midpoint 2.131 years after launch)
ramp_steepness.note: Reused measured neurology curve: the most recent launch of a disease-modifying drug into a neurodegenerative disease. Case against: Leqembi needs infusions and MRI monitoring, while votoplam is a daily oral, which argues for a faster ramp

ramp_midpoint_year.source: as ramp_steepness (Leqembi fit carried by the trontinemab seed, midpoint 2.131 years after launch)
ramp_midpoint_year.note: Trontinemab adds two years for its own later launch; here forecast_start_year already sits at the first full year, so the launch-relative midpoint is used
